paragraphs: Here's what I see in this passage, friend. Ahaziah doesn't just wander into trouble. His mother was "his counselor in wickedness," and after his father died, the house of Ahab became his counselors too (2 Chronicles 22:3-4). The text says it was "to his destruction" (2 Chronicles 22:4). Whoever sits in your ear is steering your life, and he let the wrong voices drive.

Now watch how this lands. Ahaziah follows their counsel, goes out to fight, and then goes down to visit a wounded ally, and the text says his "downfall came from God" (2 Chronicles 22:5-7). A friendly visit, and it's the very place it all comes to a head. I think that should make every one of us ask who we're listening to, because the road a counselor points you down is the road you end up on.

And then there's that burial. They put Ahaziah to death, but they bury him, saying, "He is the grandson of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart" (2 Chronicles 22:9). Look at that, friend. A grandfather's faith was still being remembered, even when the grandson wasn't walking in it. So fill your ears with the Word, and pick counselors who point you to the LORD, because that's the voice worth following.
